newsitem.title: UK: Dlr ends lower in Europe, Swiss franc recovers.
newsitem.headline: Dlr ends lower in Europe, Swiss franc recovers.

text.p: The dollar closed a touch weaker in lacklustre European trading, keeping to narrow ranges of less than a pfenning and less than a yen.
A spate of stronger-than-expected German economic data on Thursday, a stronger yen and a recovery of the Swiss franc have added to the more subdued dollar tone in the last few sessions.

"The dollar had a fairly dull session, while the Swiss franc had quite a good day after its bad performance earlier in the week," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank in London. "The dollar is generally softer. It's run out of steam throughout the week."
At 1540 GMT the dollar was at 1.6837/43 marks and 122.55/60 yen, compared with 1.6865/75 and 122.72/82 in late European trading on Thursday.
The Swiss franc regained some poise, buoyed by buying of Swiss francs for yen, dealers said.
After sinking to a three-year low of 1.4907 Swiss francs against the dollar on Wednesday, the Swiss currency has risen some 1.5 percent against the dollar and also gained on the mark.
Dealers said Swiss/yen bids put pressure on mark/Swiss and also weighed on dollar/mark. Dollar/Swiss was at 1.4665/70 francs from 1.4760/66 in late European trading on Thursday.
Mark/Swiss franc dropped to 87.11/15 from 87.56/57 at the previous European close.

Earlier comments by Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke that Germany was unlikely to meet the EMU deficit criterion in 1997 also hit dollar/mark, dealers said. Welteke said Germany was still expected to be part of EMU at the onset from 1999.

The dollar's sharp fall against the yen on Thursday pushed risk reversals on dollar/yen options into favouring yen calls rather than yen puts. The risk of a dollar/yen shakeout also underpinned implied volatility on dollar/yen options, while dollar/mark vols eased back.
However, dealers said consolidation was the dominant force on both dollar/yen and dollar/mark.
"The dollar is still well supported," said a senior trader at a Swiss bank in London. "Especially on dollar/yen the market got quite long, so now it's time for some moderation."
Against the yen, the key level to watch on the downside was 122.30 yen, the overnight low, ahead of a previous support zone at 122.30, the trader said.
Another market focus was the European Union's approval of Italy's eurotax, a one-off measure in 1997 to cut Italy's budget deficit in its drive to join the single currency.

The ruling bolstered Italian hopes to be part of EMU from its start but had little net effect on the lira as approval had been expected. Mark/lira was at 988.50/80 from 987.00/45 in late European trade on Thursday.
Focus next week will be Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey Hawkins testimony on the U.S. economy on Wednesday and Thursday.

Analysts said a benign speech could fire up markets. "Greenspan's testimony will provide the main focus next week for the dollar," said Ferridge. "The market will be watching for indications from him whether U.S. rates will be raised."
Greenspan made a speech on bank regulatory issues on Friday but stayed clear of commenting on the economy or the dollar.

Dealers said the recovery of Wall Street stocks after a 93-point fall in the Dow Jones industrial average on Thursday gave some comfort to the dollar. -- Astrid Zweynert London newsroom + 44 171 542 7792
